variants.title: Prairie Plant Survival Reading
variants.student_facing_instructions: Read the passage about prairie plants. Find the section that explains how roots help plants stay alive during dry weather. Write one complete sentence explaining how roots help the plant.
variants.teacher_notes: Standard literacy task. Ensure students are focused on the relationship between root structure and environmental adaptation.

variants.title: Plant Roots: Reading & Drawing
variants.student_facing_instructions: Read the short story about plants. Look at the pictures of roots. Circle the word 'roots'. Use this sentence starter to write your answer: 'Roots help plants because...'
variants.teacher_notes: Use bilingual word walls for 'roots' and 'dry'. Provide visual step-cards showing the reading -> circling -> writing process. Supports Amira, Daniyal, and Imani.

variants.title: Step-by-Step: Prairie Plants
variants.student_facing_instructions: Step 1: Read the first paragraph. Check with a partner. Step 2: Find and underline the word 'roots'. Step 3: Read the second paragraph. Step 4: Write your sentence about roots.
variants.teacher_notes: Break the task into discrete milestones to assist with pacing and focus. Useful for Brody (transitions) and students needing routine support.

variants.title: Small Group Science Discovery
variants.student_facing_instructions: Listen to the story about prairie plants. We will look at pictures of different roots together. Tell me one way roots help a plant stay healthy in the sun.
variants.teacher_notes: Designed for Ms. Fehr to run in the morning. Focus on oral comprehension and vocabulary building. Can use concrete models of roots (e.g., string or actual plant) to support Elena and EAL learners.
required_materials: Plant root models or real plant

variants.title: Prairie Plant Expert Challenge
variants.student_facing_instructions: After reading about prairie plants, research or brainstorm: How might a plant's roots change if it lived in a rainforest instead of a dry prairie? Write a short comparison.
variants.teacher_notes: Open-ended challenge for students like Chantal or Wesley. Encourages higher-order thinking and application of science concepts to different environments.
